question: What is the value of (1 + tan² theta)/(1 + cot² theta) ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use identities: 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ

Expression = sec²θ / cosec²θ

= (1/cos²θ) ÷ (1/sin²θ)

= sin²θ / cos²θ = tan²θ

**∴ Answer = tan²θ**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(1 + tan²θ) ÷ (1 + cot²θ)

**Formula used:**

1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ

**Calculation:**

⇒ = sec²θ ÷ cosec²θ

⇒ = (1/cos²θ) ÷ (1/sin²θ)

⇒ = sin²θ / cos²θ

⇒ = tan²θ

**∴ The correct answer is tan²θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

1 + tan²θ = sec²θ and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ

Reciprocal Identities

secθ = 1/cosθ and cosecθ = 1/sinθ

Trigonometric Ratio

tanθ = sinθ / cosθ

Simplification Tip

Convert everything into sin and cos for easy cancellation.
